content.title: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust files for IPO
content.text: Erik IsaksonA newly formed company, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, filed a prospectus for an IPO on Friday. The new entity is " focused on acquiring and owning mission-critical data center assets that power the modern digital economy," it said. The company intends to qualify as a real estate investment trust but is currently considered a "blind pool," as it hasn't yet acquired any data center assets. It expects to trade under the BXDC ticker. The company will be externally managed by BX REIT, an affiliate of Blackstone (BX), an investment manager with $1.3T of assets under management as of Dec. 31, 2025. Blackstone Real Estate, founded in 1991, is the world's largest owner of commercial real estate, with $319B of investor capital under management as of the end of 2025. The infrastructure group was founded in 2017 and manages $77B of capital across digital infrastructure, energy, and transportation assets as of Dec. 31, 2025. BXDC plans to invest in digital infrastructure primarily in top data center markets that exhibit strong supply-demand dynamics. Furthermore, it will aim to acquire assets with fixed, annual rent escalators and favorable tenant expense reimbursement structures to generate predictable yields and stable cash flows. Blackstone estimates the industry represents a substantial investment opportunity with an estimated $1T total addressable stabilized data center market expected over the next five years. An affiliate of Blackstone (BX) has indicated interest in buying an undisclosed number of shares in the new REIT, the filing said. The joint lead book-running managers include Goldman Sachs (GS), Citigroup (C), and Morgan Stanley (MS). Bloomberg News reported earlier that Blackstone was planning a $2B IPO for an acquisition company that will buy data centers. The filing had no estimates for the potential amount of proceeds from the proposed offering.
